key_insight: IndustrialRemembr extends NVIDIA ReMEmbR from individual robots to a shared spatiotemporal memory for robot fleets. It aims to make warehouse observations reusable while reducing server-side computation.
problem_solved: Understanding recurring warehouse problems, such as aisle blockages, can require reviewing video from many robots across multiple shifts. Preserving these observations as searchable semantic memory creates substantial computation, communication, and storage costs.
method: Extend NVIDIA ReMEmbR to support shared memory across a robot fleet.
Organize observations by location and time to support analysis across robots and shifts.
Use scene descriptions to reduce server-side computation; the provided abstract is truncated before implementation details are given.
impact: Shared fleet memory could help practitioners investigate recurring operational issues without manually reviewing large video archives. The provided excerpt does not include measured efficiency gains or evaluation results.
visual_elements: Warehouse map showing multiple robots contributing observations to a shared memory.
Location-linked timeline illustrating repeated aisle blockages across shifts.
Conceptual pipeline: robot observations → scene descriptions → shared spatiotemporal memory → operational questions.
Compute, network, and storage icons highlighting the costs of retaining fleet observations.
paper_title: Industrial ReMEmbR: Scaling Spatiotemporal Memory to Robot Fleets
paper_authors: Jad Yammine, Malek Wahidi, Abrar Anwar, Yan Chang, Mihir Acharya
